title: The bus speaks TCP between boxes and on Windows
intention: The bus carries messages over TCP between boxes and on Windows, while staying on Unix sockets inside a Linux box, so a device on akiendell can reach a bus and the buses on two boxes can reach each other.
why: Python on Windows has no socket.AF_UNIX (measured 2026-11-04 on akiendell: the web server died at cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py:95), so no device on a Windows box can reach any bus; and buses on two boxes (outline 5.4.2.8.1) can only reach each other over the network. Akien 2026-11-04: 'yes please' (outline 5.4.2.11.4).
traces_to: Outline 5.4.2.8 (one bus per cairn instance, extended across hosts), 5.4.2.8.1 (a bus per box, the buses talk) and 5.4.2.11.4 (TCP between boxes and on Windows); Telos: running multiple heavy tasks at once across Akien's boxes; Law 3 (the transport choice is settled by measuring, 5.4.2.11).
how: Give the bus an address that is either a Unix socket path or host:port. server.py:523 also listens on TCP (localhost on Windows, the LAN for box-to-box) beside bus.sock; remote.py exchange() picks the transport from the address (AF_UNIX where it exists and the bus is on this box, TCP otherwise). Same wire format (one JSON request, one JSON reply), so callers do not change. A gate for TCP: a shared instance token in ~/.cairn, since file mode 0600 no longer gates. Measure TCP loopback latency against the 50 us Unix socket number (5.4.2.11.1). BUILDER BRIEF: A Haiku builder needs: (1) the files: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py (listener at :523), cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/__main__.py:23, cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py (exchange at :87-104, _spawn :147, _setsid :197); (2) the port: env CAIRN_BUS_TCP_PORT, default 7419 (unassigned by IANA), checked free at build; (3) the selection rule above, verbatim; (4) that the wire format must not change; (5) the Windows spawn flags DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW as in launchers/superclaude _sc_spawn_detached; (6) the gate, from the answer to open-4d72b5d4dbe0; (7) proofs in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/ and cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/, a tooth that forces the TCP path on Linux (AF_UNIX hidden) so it is provable here; (8) the latency bench is scratch today (5.4.2.11.1), so record numbers in the ticket, not a new tool.
falsifier: Done when (a) on akiendell, a fresh python using cairn.tools.bus_client.remote.RemoteBus().list() gets an answer from a bus it lazily started, over TCP 127.0.0.1, no AF_UNIX error; (b) from akiendell a request reaches the bus on akiendelllinux over the LAN under the gate open-4d72b5d4dbe0 picks, and an ungated caller is refused; (c) on Linux the Unix-socket p50 round trip stays within 10% of the 50 us measured at outline 5.4.2.11.1, and TCP loopback is measured and recorded. Horizon: the first box-to-box message. Wrong intent if Akien picks ssh tunnelling for everything (then (b) is a tunnel, not a LAN listener).
decisions: Unix sockets stay the transport inside a Linux box; TCP is added only where Unix cannot go (Windows, box to box).
The wire format (one JSON request, one JSON reply) does not change; callers do not change.
remote.py picks AF_UNIX when socket has it and the bus is on this box, else TCP.
On Windows the bus listens on 127.0.0.1 only; the home box listens on the LAN only under the gate open-4d72b5d4dbe0 settles.
remote.py spawns the bus on Windows with DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW, as launchers/superclaude _sc_spawn_detached does.
A proof tooth forces the TCP path on Linux (AF_UNIX hidden) so the Windows path is provable on this box.
Bus-to-bus routing by name is out of scope: a follow-on ticket.
